records.title: 10-K

records.title: 10-K
records.text: ◦Gained sales momentum at Soma: Soma generated comparable sales growth for the last seven months in fiscal 2020, and according to market research firm NPD, Group Inc., for the 12 months ended January 2021, Soma’s growth exceeded that of the U.S. apparel market and the market leader for non-sport bras and panties, and was in the top five brands overall in the sleepwear market.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The decrease in gross margin rate primarily reflects lower maintained margin including pre-tax inventory write-offs of $55 million, or 4.2% of net sales, the impact of temporary store closures or stores operating at reduced hours which resulted in deleverage of fixed occupancy costs, and store impairment charges of $23 million, or 1.8% of net sales.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: For fiscal 2020, gross margin was $184 million, or 13.9% of net sales, compared to $702 million, or 34.4% of net sales, in fiscal 2019.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: During fiscal 2020, the Company experienced varying degrees of business disruptions as a result of the pandemic, which had a material adverse impact on our business operations and operating results and operating cash flows during fiscal 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Net sales decreased $1,376.2 million, or 21.3%, in fiscal 2020 compared to fiscal 2019.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: However beginning in the first quarter of our fiscal year 2020, as a result of COVID-19 related closures, we excluded stores from the comparable sales base that were closed for 14 consecutive days or more and where curbside delivery was not available to customers.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Improved inventory management drove a significant increase in inventory turns and as a result, in working capital, while an intense focus on organization structure and expense reductions yielded a $408.5 million or 21.2% reduction in reported Selling, General and Administrative costs in fiscal 2020 as compared to fiscal 2019.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: During the early stages of the global pandemic and subsequent period of temporary closures, we took steps to continue to serve our customers via our e-commerce platform including, but not limited to enhancing our online capabilities and offering curbside pick-up options while also lowering our purchase and expense levels to correspond with the lower demand.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: In fiscal 2020, cash flow from operating activities was an inflow of $123.7 million, an increase of $538.2 million compared to an outflow of $414.5 million during the same period last year.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: While our net sales decreased 32%, which reflected temporary store closures during the first half of 2020, we are encouraged by the continued sequential improvement in topline trends during the second half.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: For the year, net loss was $690, or $4.39 per diluted share.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Ending inventory as of January 30, 2021 decreased 3.0% compared with prior year.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The average sales price at both Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack decreased primarily due to customer shopping behavior and category shift.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Net cash used in investing activities decreased by $562 between 2020 and 2019 due to a decrease in capital expenditures as the prior period included investments in our Nordstrom NYC store, as well as supply chain costs related to our market strategy.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Gross margin dollars increased $382.7 million and gross margin rate increased 60 basis points to 40.3% of net sales.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Comparable sales for stores open at least fifteen months, plus our e-commerce operations, increased $816.1 million, or 16.1%.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Inventory of $940.3 million represented a $19.0 million increase, or 2.1%, from 2019.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The combined gain on sale of distribution centers and associated consulting and other expenses increased our operating profit by $459.1 million and increased our diluted earnings per share by approximately $8.75 per share.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Operating profit increased $521.7 million to $856.5 million.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Total net sales decreased approximately 14% for Fiscal 2020 as compared to Fiscal 2019, primarily driven by temporary store closures and a decline in traffic as compared to the previous year as a result of COVID-19.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: In light of store closures related to COVID-19, the Company has not disclosed comparable sales for Fiscal 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The Company has experienced other material impacts as a result of COVID-19, including, but not limited to, deferred tax valuation allowances, long-lived asset impairment, adjustments of the carrying amount of inventory and changes in the effectiveness of its hedging instruments.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Reduced expenses to better align operating costs with sales;

records.title: 10-K
records.text: This section provides a discussion of the Company’s financial condition, changes in financial condition and liquidity as of January 30, 2021, which includes (i) an analysis of changes in cash flows for Fiscal 2020 as compared to Fiscal 2019, (ii) an analysis of liquidity, including the availability under credit facilities, payments of dividends, and outstanding debt and covenant compliance, (iii) a summary of contractual and other obligations as of January 30, 2021 and (iv) a discussion related to actions taken during Fiscal 2020 to preserve liquidity in light of COVID-19.
